facts.statement: Itemirus was a dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur that lived during the Turonian age of the Late Cretaceous period in Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: Itemirus is a genus of dromaeosaurid theropod dinosaur from the Turonian aged Bissekty Formation of the Late Cretaceous period of Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: The only known fossil of Itemirus is a small, damaged braincase discovered in 1958 near the village of Itemir in Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: Itemirus is known from a single small, damaged fossil braincase or neurocranium, in 1958 found near the village of Itemir at the Dzharakuduk escarpment in layers of the Bissekty Formation.

facts.statement: The species Itemirus medullaris was named and described by Sergei Kurzanov in 1976.
facts.quote: The type species, Itemirus medullaris, was named and described by Sergei Kurzanov in 1976.

facts.statement: Analysis of the braincase suggests Itemirus had good vision and balance due to large brain lobes.
facts.quote: Solo la bóveda craneal se ha encontrado, lo que permite hacer estimaciones sobre el tamaño del cerebro, que dan evidencia que tenía buena visión y balance a partir de los grandes lóbulos cerebrales.

facts.statement: A 2014 study placed the genus Itemirus within the subfamily Dromaeosaurinae based on additional fossil material.
facts.quote: In 2014, during a study assigning more material to Itemirus, it was found that the genus could be placed in Dromaeosaurinae in a phylogeny.

facts.statement: Kurzanov originally assigned Itemirus to its own family, Itemiridae, based on similarities to both tyrannosaurs and dromaeosaurs.
facts.quote: Kurzanov noted anatomical similarities to the Tyrannosauridae and the Dromaeosauridae; he assigned Itemirus to a separate Itemiridae.

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz suggested that Itemirus might be a member of Tyrannosauroidea.
facts.quote: Thomas Holtz sugirió que es miembro de Tyrannosauroidea.

facts.statement: Itemirus lived between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago during the Turonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The species name 'medullaris' refers to the medulla oblongata, the part of the brain protected by the fossilized braincase.
rejected.quote: The specific name refers to the medulla oblongata, the part of the brain encased by the partial braincase.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'refers to the medulla oblongata the part of'

rejected.statement: A 2009 cladistic analysis by Longrich and Currie classified Itemirus as a velociraptorine.
rejected.quote: In 2009, Nicholas Longrich and Philip J. Currie included Itemirus in a cladistic analysis of internal dromaeosaurid relationships and found it to be a velociraptorine.
